KIMBA & AFRICA ENJOY A SCRATCH. Seven tigers removed from tiny cages in Circo Rey Gitano in Guatemala are in an ADI Temporary Rescue Unit (ADI TRU) while preparations are made to take them to a new life at the ADI Wildlife Sanctuary. This is a temporary hospital facility where the cages used to remove the tigers from the circus are joined together to give the animals more space.  Already the tigers have more space than they had in the circus and in some cases, more than three times the space. The animals can be separated for feeding, veterinary treatment and for cage cleaning – a cage is being cleaned in the background. We will soon be adding exercise enclosures with small pools.  The ADI Wildlife Sanctuary in South Africa will be their forever home with huge natural enclosures  – each tiger will have at least 10,000 square meters / 107,639 square feet. All seven tigers were successfully removed from the circus by Guatemala’s animal welfare division, Unidad de Bienestar Animal (UBA) and wildlife department Consejo Nacional de Areas Protegidas (CONAP) and police.  All are well at the ADI TRU and this has been verified by officials and the Guatemala media. These tigers deserve some freedom for their final years, don’t let them be forced back into the tiny circus cages they have endured for years. Speak up for the tigers. #StopCircusSuffering
